Final for Publication

17-13-0303-C(1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans — 1114-1118 North California Avenue, Chicago, IL

Proposed Zoning: B2-3 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District
Lot Area: 1118 North California Avenue — 3,014 (6,029.8 sq. ft. total)

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant intends to divide the single zoning lot into two (2) separate
zoning lots so that the newly created lot at 1118 North California Avenue
can be developed with a new four-story, five (5) dwelling unit residential
building. The proposed building will measure 42.54 ft. in height and feature
three (3) private rooftop decks.. The subject lot is a Transit Served Location
and will be supported three (3) off-street surface parking spaces at the rear
of that lot. The height and footprint of the existing one-story residential
building at 1114 North California Avenue will remain without change.
Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-0303-D optional Administrative Adjustment and
Variation and pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-EE of the Chicago Zoning
Ordinance, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the off-street parking
requirement for a Transit Served Location from 100% (5 parking spaces) to
60% (3 parking spaces) for the proposed building at 1118 North California
Avenue and is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Chicago
Zoning Code, for the attached plans.

(A) The Project’s Floor Area Ratio:
a. 1118 North California Avenue: 7,136 square feet (2.37 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.):
a. 1118 North California Avenue: 602.8 square feet per D.U.
(5 residential units)

(C)  *The amount of off-street parking:
a. 1118 North California Avenue: 3 parking spaces

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location (Division Bus
Route). Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the
off-street parking requirement from 100% (five (5) parking spaces) to 60% (three
(3) parking spaces) at 1118 North California Avenue.

(D) — Setbacks:
a. 1118 North California Avenue:
i. Front Setback: 3.5 feet
ii. Side Setbacks:
North Side: 0 feet
South Side: 3 feet
iii. Rear Setback: 30 feet

(E) Building Height:
a. 1118 North California Avenue: 42.54 feet

Final for Publication

Sec. 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 500 linear feet of the Division Avenue CTA Bus
Line Corridor roadway segment. The proposed residential building containing five (5)
residential units will be supported by three (3) off-street parking spaces. Pursuant to
Section 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to permit a reduction in the number of
required off-street parking spaces, from five (5) parking spaces to three (3) parking spaces.

2. The proposed building design complies with the main building door and entryway design
standards provided by Sec. 17-4-0504. The proposed building will have a front setback of
3 feet from the subject lot’s front property line along North California Avenue to align with
the footprints of the neighboring buildings on the block. The building’s first floor was
designed with windows facing the sidewalk located along North California Avenue.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
residential building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location along the Division CTA bus route. The Applicant believes the development of an
underutilized and unimproved lot will improve conditions in the subject area for residents
and other commuters traveling in the subject area.

4. The proposed residential building will contain a total of five (5) residential units. The
proposed building will be supported by three (3) off-street parking spaces. The Applicant
is seeking administrative approval to permit the off-street parking reduction pursuant to the
eTOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed residential building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will improve an unimproved
lot with a new multi-unit residential building, which will provide new residential housing
to meet multi-unit market demand. Based on the subject property’s proximity to a
designated CTA bus route (Division CTA Bus Line), the Applicant believes the project
provides transit options and otherwise complies with the Travel Demand Study and
Management Plan rules promulgated by the Department of Transportation by serving an

area in need.
